title: Find Servers That Handled Most Number of Requests
summary: Given k servers numbered from 0 to k-1, each with infinite computational capacity but handling only one request at a time, requests are assigned according to a specific algorithm.
statement: Given k servers numbered from 0 to k-1, each with infinite computational capacity but handling only one request at a time, requests are assigned according to a specific algorithm. For the i-th request, if all servers are busy, the request is dropped. If the (i % k)-th server is available, it handles the request; otherwise, the next available server is found by wrapping around the list of servers. The goal is to identify the server(s) that handled the most number of requests successfully. Return the IDs of the busiest server(s) in any order.
constraints: There are k servers and strictly increasing arrival times; arrival and load have equal length.
Request i prefers i mod k and then the next available server cyclically; drop it if all servers are busy.
Return every server handling the maximum number of requests, in increasing index order.
reference_solution:
def busiest_servers(k,arrival,load):
    import heapq
    available=list(range(k));busy=[];count=[0]*k
    for index,(time,duration) in enumerate(zip(arrival,load)):
        while busy and busy[0][0]<=time:
            _,server=heapq.heappop(busy);heapq.heappush(available,index+(server-index)%k)
        if not available:continue
        server=heapq.heappop(available)%k;count[server]+=1
        heapq.heappush(busy,(time+duration,server))
    best=max(count)
    return [server for server,value in enumerate(count) if value==best]
hints: Maintain busy servers by finish time and available servers by cyclic preference order.
Release finished servers using shifted keys relative to the current request index.
Pop the smallest shifted available key, reduce modulo k, count it, and push its finish time.
The shift maps cyclic order starting at i mod k into ordinary increasing heap order.

Each request finds its preferred server available; server zero handles two and is busiest.
